root_cause_label: Brittle Shell Pipeline for Stateful Log Parsing
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent used 'grep -A 3 | paste -d| - - -' to extract the top 3 frames per trace, a strategy that misaligns when trace frames span fewer than 3 lines or when multi-line wrapped frame text exists, producing incorrect unique-site counts; the agent then only fixed a cosmetic 'in' prefix issue and never recognized the fundamental logic flaw.
t_err_evidence: In step 3, the agent writes the core pipeline 'grep -A 3 '^[0-9][0-9]*$' log.stack | grep -v '^[0-9][0-9]*$' | grep -v '^--$' | sed ... | paste -d '|' - - -', which assumes every trace contributes exactly 3 non-separator output lines. The head -n 20 output from step 2 already showed a single trace with at least 18 frames, and the log lines can also wrap (e.g., line 63-64 in step 2 shows a single frame split across two terminal lines). The 'paste -d| - - -' groups consecutive lines in fixed triplets regardless of actual trace boundaries, causing systematic misalignment.
t_commit_evidence: After step 3 executes './analyze.sh > /app/output.txt' with the flawed pipeline, the output file is written with incorrect data. All subsequent steps only fix formatting cosmetics or confirm the result; the core logic is never revised, locking in the wrong output.
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on the unverified assumption that every stack trace in the log contributes exactly 3 lines of frame output after filtering out separator lines and grep context separators ('--'). The head output at step 2 already showed a trace with many more than 3 frames, but the agent did not reason about what 'grep -A 3' would produce for such multi-frame traces or how 'paste -d| - - -' would mis-group the resulting lines.
forewarning_evidence: Step 2's 'head -n 20 log.stack' output shows the first trace alone has at least 18 frames (the output continues well past the first few frames), making it visually clear that traces are not uniformly 3 frames long. This contradicts the 'grep -A 3' strategy chosen in step 3.
